blindSummary:
This is an overseas collectivity of a distant metropolitan state, largely self-governing; the metropolitan state's civil law applies here. Culturally significant: an indigenous third-gender tradition long predates colonisation and is socially embedded in local island culture, providing an informal acceptance unusual within the collectivity's own official legal culture.

The evidence base for this territory is inherited from the administering metropolitan state's legal framework; the underlying documentation sits in that state's own record, so territory-specific legal facts below are metropolitan facts applied here unchanged.
blindOutOfScope: Overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations are noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: News-site feature (Jan 2018): trans women incarcerated in the administering state on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area and are punished beyond their alleged crimes - relevant to this territory because it is an overseas collectivity applying the metropolitan state's law.

The metropolitan state's detention-watchdog opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty (its framework applies in this territory): serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all places of detention.

Online-encyclopedia page on transgender rights in the territory's main island: the metropolitan state's anti-discrimination law applies here (gender-identity protections since 2012, hate-crime provisions since 2017, conversion-therapy ban since 2022); legal gender recognition without restrictions; culturally, an indigenous third-gender role predates colonisation, while contemporary trans identities face varying stigma; transphobic violence and employment discrimination pushing some trans women into sex work persist.

LGBTQ+ travel site (April 2025): a feature arguing the destination earns its place on every LGBTQ+ travel list without needing Pride-branded reassurances - openness is described as ingrained in the local culture; the traditional third-gender role and contemporary trans identities are visible in daily life; 118 islands with direct flights from major cities.

Regional public broadcaster (Dec 2023): the territory held its first international colloquium on LGBTQIA+ rights, framed around local voices and customary ways of the surrounding island region, at the territory's university - with government, church and regional participants; it recalled that indigenous third-gender roles, known under different local names across neighbouring island societies, are a well-entrenched, accepted part of society.

Gay-travel guide for the territory: 'a relaxed, gay-welcoming island culture' across the main island, the famous lagoon destinations and the territory's 118 islands - travel-oriented assessment of the destination.
